newsitem.title: UK: Tanker owners urged to monitor loading operations.
newsitem.headline: Tanker owners urged to monitor loading operations.

text.p: Tanker owners are being urged by their industry association to monitor loading and discharge operations to ensure the validity of claims for cargo loss.
Intertanko, the International Association of Independent Tanker Owners, said: "There is a need for an increased awareness on the part of owners to enable them to assess the validity of such claims."
It said: "The majority of claims often appear to be spurious and are successfully defended."
But the association added: "However, the claimant usually does have a genuine shortfall in commercial terms, even though no loss has occurred that is attributable to fault on the vessel's part."

Intertanko said oil cargo shortage claims were largely unheard of before 1973 when rising crude prices meant the standard insurance deductible of 0.5 percent on an average cargo of 1 million barrels could cost an oil company about US$ 150,000.
However, it said this allowance had now been rejected in the US and differences of more than 0.25 percent between loading and discharge quantities should be protested against by owners.
Intertanko advised owners to take several preventative measures to reduce claims.

They included paying careful attention to onboard surveys prior to loading and discharge to limit the scope of 'paper losses' and making sure that Remaining on Board certificates showed oil not discharged was not pumpable.

The association also urged owners to be aware of the potential for evaporation losses in transit and during loading operations and to ascertain any inaccuracies in current or updated petroleum measurement tables.
Intertanko issued its updated advice in a new edition of its publication Oil Cargo Losses and Problems with Measurement.
